note: Lets a backend-unreachable (local/firewalled) site poll the Sync Core for queued requests instead of receiving pushes. Real artifacts: the Drush command cms_content_sync_private_environment:poll (cspep), a cron handler, and the route cms_content_sync_private_environment.private_environment (/admin/config/services/cms_content_sync/private-environment). No config/permission/plugins. Medium introspects the registered route on the live site; hard is an enable-the-integration task (safe to toggle - no dependents). No backend needed.

evals.prompt: What problem does cms_content_sync_private_environment solve, and by what mechanism (push vs poll) does it work?
evals.expected_output: It lets a site the Sync Core backend cannot reach inbound (e.g. a local/firewalled dev environment) take part in syndication by polling the backend for queued requests instead of receiving inbound push calls.

evals.prompt: Which Drush command does cms_content_sync_private_environment provide to poll the backend, what is its alias, and what does its limit argument accept?
evals.expected_output: cms_content_sync_private_environment:poll (alias cspep); the limit argument is 'watch', 'all', or a fixed number, with options --pollInterval (watch mode, default 15s) and --host.

evals.prompt: Besides the Drush command, how else can cms_content_sync_private_environment process pending sync requests, and what authentication must be configured for Content Sync for it to work?
evals.expected_output: It also processes requests on cron (hook_cron calls RequestHandlerController::processRequests when enabled). It requires Basic Auth to be enabled and configured for Content Sync.

evals.prompt: On this running site, the cms_content_sync_private_environment module is enabled. Inspect the site's registered routes and give the URL path of its private-environment request handler route.

This Drupal site runs behind a firewall so the Content Sync backend cannot reach it directly. Enable the Content Sync submodule that lets this site participate in syndication by polling the backend for queued requests.
evals.expected_output: The cms_content_sync_private_environment module is enabled (e.g. drush en cms_content_sync_private_environment -y), registering its poll command, cron handler and private-environment route.
